Test Description: Verifies PCIe device enumeration by performing link training, configuring cache coherency via the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register, polling link-up status on both SII interfaces, reading the device Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, enabling IO/Memory/Bus Master access in TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG, programming memory base addresses, performing BAR sizing on BAR0_REG, BAR1_REG, SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG, SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG, MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG, and PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG for both root complex and endpoint devices, disabling cache coherency, and polling a synchronization register for test completion.

Enable cache coherency by performing read-modify-write operations on the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIe controllers, setting the required bit fields. 4. Wait for the coherency configuration to take effect. 5. Poll the SII0 link status register until the link-up condition is detected. 6. Poll the SII1 link status register until the link-up condition is detected. 7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC settings. 8. Read the Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG and verify the device is detected. 9. Enable IO space, memory space, and bus master in TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG. 10. Program memory base addresses for both controllers. 11. Write enable values to system-level configuration registers. 12. Program actual base addresses into the BAR and bridge window registers for both endpoint and root complex. 15. Read back all programmed BAR and bridge registers to verify. 16. Poll the synchronization register until the expected completion value is received. 17. End the test upon successful synchronization.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe DMA write and read data transfer operations across four channels on the configured dual-mode controller. The same sequence is repeated for DMA read transfers on all four channels via DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. The interrupt handler reads DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF to determine which channels completed, then clears the interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF. The test validates that all eight DMA transfers complete successfully via interrupt signaling.

For each of the four DMA write channels, program the channel with source address, destination address, and transfer length, then trigger the transfer via DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF and wait for interrupt-driven completion. 13. End the test after all DMA transfers complete successfully.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe register reset default values and read-write functionality across DBI controller registers, SII registers, and PHY registers for both PCIe controllers. The test first reads all registers and validates that they contain the expected default values after reset. It then performs write-read verification using multiple test patterns, writing known values to MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF, and corresponding SII and PHY registers, then reading back and comparing against expected values with appropriate write masks applied. The test reports pass or fail based on accumulated error counts across all register checks.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Perform reset value verification by reading all DBI controller registers for both PCIe controllers and comparing against expected default values. 2. Read all SII registers for both controllers and verify they match expected default values. 3. Configure PHY reset control for both controllers. 4. Read all PHY registers for both controllers with appropriate bit extraction and verify they match expected default values. 5. Perform write-read verification using multiple test patterns (all-ones, alternating bits, inverse alternating bits). 6. For each test pattern, write the pattern to all DBI controller registers including MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, and UTILITY_OFF for both controllers. 7. Write masked test patterns to all SII registers for both controllers. 8. Write masked PHY-specific test patterns to all PHY registers for both controllers. 9. Read back all DBI controller registers and verify the written values match. 10. Read back all SII registers and verify the masked written values match. 11. Read back all PHY registers with bit extraction and verify the masked written values match. 12. Report pass if no mismatches are detected across all register checks; otherwise report fail.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) All DBI controller registers for both PCIe controllers read back their expected default values of zero after reset. (2) All SII registers for both controllers read back their expected default values of zero after reset. (3) All PHY registers for both controllers read back their expected default values of zero after reset, with correct 16-bit extraction applied. (4) For each of the three write-read test patterns, all DBI controller registers including MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, and UTILITY_OFF read back the exact written value. (5) All SII registers read back the correctly masked written value. (6) All PHY registers read back the correctly masked written value with proper bit extraction. (7) The test ends with finish(0) indicating zero accumulated errors across all checks.
Remarks: The testcase validates three categories of registers: DBI controller registers, SII interface registers, and PHY registers across both PCIe controllers. Write masks are applied for SII and PHY registers to account for read-only or reserved bit fields. PHY registers require 16-bit extraction based on address alignment. The PHY reset control register is written before each PHY register access phase. Three test patterns are used for write-read verification covering all-ones, alternating-bit, and inverse alternating-bit patterns. SII and PHY registers could not be mapped to the provided specification. Error counts are tracked separately and combined for the final pass/fail determination.
